conversation.user: Who is Stacy D. VanDeveer and what research did he lead at SSL?
conversation.assistant: Stacy D. VanDeveer served as a principal investigator on a research team [1]. The provided documents do not contain further information regarding his specific professional title or biographical details. Stacy D. VanDeveer led the research project titled "LEARNING FROM THE MASSACHUSETTS MUNICIPAL VULNERABILITY PREPAREDNESS (MVP) PROGRAM IN THE GREATER BOSTON REGION" [1]. The objective of this study was to understand conditions in and across municipalities within the Greater Boston metropolitan area regarding the Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness (MVP) program [1].

conversation.user: What was the research on the Massachusetts MVP program about?
conversation.assistant: The research project titled "LEARNING FROM THE MASSACHUSETTS MUNICIPAL VULNERABILITY PREPAREDNESS (MVP) PROGRAM IN THE GREATER BOSTON REGION" had the objective of understanding conditions in and across municipalities within the Greater Boston metropolitan area regarding the Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness (MVP) program [1]. In 2020, more than 80% of Massachusetts cities and towns had participated in the MVP program [1]. The findings from this research are being used to improve program design to support equitable inclusion [1].

conversation.user: What is the East Boston study that VanDeveer's team worked on?
conversation.assistant: The research project titled "CONDITIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR EQUITABLE CLIMATE RESILIENCE IN EAST BOSTON" examined environmental justice concerns and sought to generate a better understanding of how these concerns apply to climate planning for residents through a justice lens [1]. This study utilized a framework of "just adaptation," performed secondary document analysis of existing resilience plans, and developed recommendations through partnerships with local residents and organizations. Additionally, Patricio Belloy, a student working with Professor Stacy D. VanDeveer, completed an assessment of resilience planning in East Boston through a climate justice lens as part of his research [2].
